flags.meaning: How Bernard of Septimania's house receives the lord: enemy, cold, neutral, warm, or ally.
Bernard's faction counts the lord an enemy.
Seen at court as one of Bernard's men.
Kept faith with the lord he had sworn to when it cost him.
Holds a written charter for the benefice.
Which side the lord took in the 830 revolt.
Stood with the emperor's party in 830.
Outlawed after the 832 revolt.
Replied warmly to Bernard's 832 letter and sent nothing.
Sent men to Pippin's 832 revolt.
Handed Bernard's letter to the emperor's men.
Refused the 832 revolt on the emperor's oath.
Warned by Ermenald's letter of Bernard's doings in 831.
Predicted the 830 revolt before it broke.
Predicted Louis's restoration in 834.
Predicted the relief army for the Spanish March would be late.
Stayed with the emperor on the Field of Lies.
Took Lothar's money on the Field of Lies.
Swore to Lothar after swearing to Louis.
Left the field when the count did.
Learned that the rumour of a Roman army was empty.
Took Pippin's part in 833.
Helped Pippin restore his father in 834.
Ermenald's trust in the lord.
Ermenald has noticed the lord knows things he should not.
Ermenald suspects the lord's knowledge is unholy.
Commended directly to the king.
Holds the villa outright.
The benefice confirmed in writing by a higher hand.
Granted a second villa.
The restored emperor's men marked him as doubtful in 834.
Raised a rank by the emperor at the court of 834.
Raised a rank by the emperor at Crémieu, 835.
Raised a rank by Pippin II at his court of 845; the villas he gave are his to lose.
The county of Autun is held by office: Roman walls, a bishop at the gate, the Saône tolls.
What the lord did when Lothar came to Chalon.
Saved Gaucelm from execution at Chalon.
Saved Gerberga from drowning at Chalon.
Swore to Lothar under threat at Chalon.
Saved Count Adalard from the flux in 837.
A rumour that the count was poisoned, with the lord's name in it.
The immediate lord, one number from 0 to 100. count_opinion and count_trust both write this.
The immediate lord's reception of him. The same number as count_trust and lord_standing.
The immediate lord's reception of him. The same number as count_opinion and lord_standing.
The church, one number from 0 to 100. Houses he has patronised warm a local asking; they are not separate tracks.
The bishop of Autun, tracked on his own only once the lord holds a county. Before that his regard is the church's.
The bishop of Autun has been split off from general church standing, because the lord holds a county.
Churchmen wonder how the lord knows what he knows.
The church counts him an enemy.
Known as a man God answers.
Known as a learned man.
Offered the monks shelter for their relics.
Relics sheltered on the estate.
Hosted the monks of Noirmoutier on their way to Tournus.
Lent carts to the monks of Tournus.
Escorted the relics of St Philibert.
Friend of the house of Tournus.
Knows the Northmen are a danger to this region.
Has the rye sorted for the dark spurs before milling.
Predicted the eclipse of 840.
Took Pippin II's part in 839.
Held to Pippin II in 840.
Submitted to Charles after Pippin II's cause.
Fled with Pippin II's party.
Betrayed Pippin II in 864.
Warned Pippin II in 864.
Pardoned by Charles in 864.
Swore to Charles the Bald in 840.
Avoided swearing to any brother in 840.
Known to have leaned to Lothar in 840.
Count Warin counts him an enemy.
Fought for Charles at Fontenoy.
Fought for Pippin II at Fontenoy.
Stayed home from Fontenoy.
Rode with Warin to Toulouse in 843.
Stood with Bernard at Toulouse in 843.
Stayed home from the Toulouse campaign.
Bernard of Septimania escaped the axe in 844.
King Charles counts him an enemy.
The crown, one number from 0 to 100. charles_favor raises it and charles_disfavor lowers it.
A step down in the crown's reception. Stored as the crown's number, not as a separate displeasure.
A step up in the crown's reception. Stored as the crown's number.
Robert the Strong survived Brissarthe.
Served in the emperor's host in 832.
Served in 839.
Took Charles's part when Aquitaine was given to him in 839.
Took the emperor's part in 832.
Named a traitor in 832.
Stayed loyal to Charles in the 858 invasion.
Swore to Louis the German in 858.
Showed sympathy for Boso's kingship.
Refused Boso's envoys.
Sworn to Richard the Justiciar.
How the Bosonids (Boso, Richard) receive the lord: enemy, cold, neutral, warm, or ally.
How the Robertians (Robert the Strong, Odo) receive the lord. No script yet writes a step; the fights and the oaths stay facts.
Whom the lord backed in the open throne of 888.
Recognised Odo as king.
Known as a shrewd judge of affairs.
Sent the count a gift in 826.
Answered the summons of 830 in person.
Rode to the restored emperor's court in 834.
Royal levies paid in coin, counted.
Royal levies refused, counted.
How the lord met the tribute of 866.
How the lord met the tribute of 877.
Famine years in which the lord fed the district.
Famine years in which the lord sold at famine prices.
Bought ruined neighbours' land in a famine.
The district's loyalty to the lord.
Under the bishop's ban.
The villa's wealth has been noticed by those who assess.
A royal missus has questioned the estate's value.
Did not answer the summons of 830.
The benefice was declared forfeit in 830 (land.ts seizes it when the claim clock runs out).
Paid the fine to keep the benefice in 830.
Took the villa under the church as precaria in 830.
Sought a royal charter in 830.
Was present when the host turned on the emperor at Compiègne.
Whispers that the lord's foreknowledge is sorcery.
Feasts sponsored at the cell.
Royal vassal duties carried out.
Royal vassal duties shirked.
Refugee households taken in across the years.
Warned the district of the Northmen before they came.
Correspondence with the learned.
Steps along Richard's road to a duchy of Burgundy.
Named among those who might take a crown in 888.
Heard Aldric's news of Aizo's revolt in 827.
Rode to the 830 muster with good horses and kit.
The opinion of Bernard the lord let fall in 828.
Met Bishop Modoin of Autun in 829.
Married into a local family to hold the villa.
The villa is held from the church as precaria.
Predicted the comet of 837 two years before it.
How the lord presented his foreknowledge of the eclipse of 840.
Served the count the rebel host installed in 830.
Holds a letter of protection from his lord while serving in the host.
Keeps stores hidden and dispersed across the manses.
Agreed to pay foragers off with a portion this season.
Escorted Bernard's kin south in 830.
Carried messages between the camps in 830.
Spoke against the land seizures at Nijmegen in 830.
Held his own men in the 830 muster when others slipped away.
Persuaded Bernard to commit to Charles at Fontenoy.
Sold grain and horses to the kings' camps at the Saône talks of 842.
Gave hospitality to envoys at the Saône talks of 842.
Offered friendship or protection to Bernard's widow Dhuoda and her sons.
Times the army fine was paid to stay home.
Set a watch on the Saône after Verdun made it a border.
Had the benefice entered under the king's promise at Coulaines.
Monks came with the church treasury and eat at the lord's table.
Returned the relics promptly when the river churches asked (885).
Sent skilled men or engineering advice to the king's bridge works (862).
The lord's part in Robert the Strong's western campaign of 866.
The lord's part in the emperor's march to Paris (886).
Argued against paying the Northmen before Paris; remembered by Odo's party.
A Duke-rank lord spent his favour to turn the Northmen away from Burgundy (886).
Took the emperor's commission to contain the Northmen in Burgundy.
Successes against the Northmen by irregular means: denial, harassment, ambush, night raids.
Had the Northmen's camp stores poisoned.
The poisoning became known; the church condemned it.
Tried to pass fouled cloth to the Northmen; a character moment, no effect on them.
The lord's part in Richard's fight at Saint-Florentin (888).
Attended Richard's wedding to Adelaide of Upper Burgundy.
Carried messages for Richard's party in the plot to crown Charles the Simple.
The lord's men guarded the fugitive king Charles on Richard's lands.
The lord's part in Richard's campaign for Sens.
The lord's part in the winter attack on the Northmen's camp (898).
The lord's answer to the Brittany summons of 845.
The lord's answer to the Brittany summons of 851.
The lord's answer to the summons for the siege of Vienne.
The lord's part in the emperor's eastern campaign of 876.
Held out with Pippin's cause after Aquitaine threw him over.
A pardoned man who sent a friendly word back to Pippin's friends in 855.
Standing with Count Girart of Vienne.
Whether the lord rode to Rome with Charles the Bald.
Known personally to Boso and Richard from the Rome journey.
Had an heir's claim to the villa written up under the capitulary of Quierzy.
Bought land and livestock cheap from neighbours ruined by a tribute levy.
Resisted Richard's seizure of Autun by arms in 880.
Stalled on the oath to Richard; the villa was claimed under the forfeiture.
How the lord answered the siege of Vienne, 880–882.
How the lord answered the royal campaign on the Saône against Boso in 880.
How a count-rank lord stood when Richard's march closed round him in 898.
Which king the lord followed when there were two, 893–897.
The lord's name was put forward for the crown in February 888.
How much of the duchy Richard has built: one for each opportunity the lord left to him (richard.ts).
Duke track: backed Rudolph as king of Upper Burgundy (888).
Duke track: married into Rudolph's house (888).
Duke track: stood behind Louis of Provence's crowning (890).
Duke track: a principal in the plot to crown Charles the Simple (892).
Duke track: sheltered Charles the Simple against the East Franks (894).
Duke track: took Sens by force (894–895).
Duke track: took the lay abbacies of Sainte-Colombe and Saint-Germain (890s).
Duke track: the king merged the lord's counties into one march (898).
Duke track: held his own assembly and judged between lords (901).
The Saracens hold Fraxinetum; the southern roads are dangerous for the rest of the game.
Sent men to escort travellers through the passes against the Saracens.
How a count-rank lord came by a mint of his own (890s).
Corresponded with Lupus of Ferrières.
Sent Nithard his own account of the war of the brothers.
Met John Scottus Eriugena at court and impressed him.
Sent a boy of the household to the school at Saint-Germain of Auxerre.
Stood witness to, or gave to, the foundation of Cluny (910).
Put a request directly to the king after hosting his court lavishly (the answer belongs to the promotion pass).
Times the lord submitted to the king to end a quarrel (at the warning, or after the attempt).
Times the king stripped the lord of honours at an assembly.
Refused the king's summons to answer charges; a rebel by his own choice.
Was excommunicated and absolved.
The king tried to have the lord killed on the road, and failed.
Accused the king openly of the attempt on his life.
Hunted the traitor among his own men after the attempt.
The king outbid the lord for the noble whose price is money; he hedges until paid again.
Elected and crowned king at the end of the king quest.
How the bishops came to crown him.
Bought his crown from the bishops; simony is said of it ever after.
It is said he bought a judgement, a ban lifted, or a bishop's voice. Enemies do not let it die.
Paid to repair and furnish a church.
Endowed a chapel or an altar.
Founded a monastery.
Founded and endowed a great church house.
Confirmed a church immunity.
Paid for a judgement.
Paid for the bishop's support.
Paid for an annulment.
Took the magnates' counter-offer: a duchy, and a Carolingian child on the throne.
How the open mishap's battle went (set by the forces tables and the refusal; read and cleared by mishaps.ts).
Mishaps that have come to a lord holding a rank above his standing.
Mishaps the lord answered decisively.
Allied with the kingdom's enemies (the Northmen, a foreign king). An aggravating factor when a rising fails.
Killed an anointed king. An aggravating factor when a rising fails.
The lord has taken a wife (marriage.ts).
Which match the lord made: the neighbour's daughter, the great family's daughter, the widow, or the woman he chose for herself alone.
Married into a great family; her brothers are his allies and her family's enemies are his.
Married for affection alone, with no land and no kin. The sworn men think less of it; his heir stands weaker for it.
Times his wife's family's quarrels have come to his door.
